description: Ambient rumor strings surfaced at inns, taverns, and campfires per zone. 3-5 per zone. Text-only content. No mechanical effects at this stage.

rumors: They say Lord-Marshal Aldric hasn't slept indoors for a month. The Ironspire's upper windows burn all night.
A patrol out of Marchkeep came back two men short and wouldn't say from what. The captain confiscated their journals.
The Assayer at Marchkeep has started asking about brooches specifically. Not any brooch. Riders' brooches.
A shepherd on the high moor swears a standing stone moved to watch him pass. He sold his flock and took the road south the next morning.
Auld Maerwyn's holt is a mile further from the road than it was last winter. The forest has opinions lately.
A coven apprentice went missing on the Verge. The Eldest isn't looking for her. That's the part that frightens the wardens.
Something drank the Singing Brook dry in three places. The water comes back at dawn but it doesn't sing anymore.
Widow Moss's cottage in Eastmile is packed up neat as a church. No struggle. Her kettle was still warm when the Rider found it.
A Caervorn patrol crossed the Verge line for the first time in living memory. They didn't find anything. That's not the same as nothing finding them.
The Compact's grain ledger is short for the third month running. Nobody's stealing it. It's just... not arriving.
Halven Orys hasn't been seen at his usual table at the Gilded Cup. His ward Thenna was there instead, dressed wrong, eating nothing.
A Golvari ambassador docked at night and nobody can find who signed his writ.
The dock-mages have started charging triple to bind cargo. They won't say why, only that 'things listen at the harbor now.'
The Asker's Stone has started asking the same question of everyone who stands on it. Kesh won't say what the question is.
Orla of Reed-End went out with the Lost Expedition and didn't come back. Her brother writes her name in wet sand every morning.
A marsh-wight swarm moved against the causeway at dusk and turned back at the halfway lantern. Swarms don't turn back.
Commander Drest hasn't held open audience in three weeks. His lieutenants hold them instead. They wear his seal but not his voice.
Something was inside the Sunken Wain. It wasn't a body. The Gravenguard cordoned the site and won't confirm they cordoned it.
The tides have started coming in at the wrong hour. The Fairgean surface more often now. They do not speak first.
A fishing boat out of the southern inlet brought back a net full of coins older than the Compact. The captain has not stopped weeping.
Something is singing under the cliffs at Black Gannet Point. The gulls have left.
A Rider with a Compact commission walked into the surf at Low Tide Cove three nights ago. He is still walking. The tide has not taken him.
The ash-wind carried a bell-note last week. There are no bells in the Reach. There haven't been for two hundred years.
A Caervorn forward scout came out of the Reach with his hair gone white and a name on his tongue he wouldn't speak. The Assayer has him now.
The glass-dunes shifted east overnight. They don't shift. They've never shifted.
A Compact caravan paid a Rider triple rate to escort them into the Reach. Nobody has ever paid triple rate to go INTO the Reach.
Something is answering the old Ardweld naming-glyphs. Brother Velm will not say whose voice is answering.
The Crow-Gibbet had a fresh body last Tuesday. Nobody in Eastmile recognized him. Nobody from the road did either.
Senna at the Bent Mare has a courier from Portmere who's taken a room indefinitely. He pays in Caervorn coin and he doesn't drink.
The Milepost at Eastmile hums louder than it used to. Brooches react to it at twenty paces now. It was ten last autumn.
A bandit crew worked Grieve's Ford for six years without a patrol catching them. They vanished in a single night. No bodies.
Lieutenant Varn has been signing orders in the Commander's name. The scribes noticed. The scribes won't say so twice.
The outer gate's third portcullis dropped on a merchant cart for no reason the wardens can name. The cart's owner is in the Dry Well now.
A Gravenguard oath-ring was found on the causeway. It belonged to a scout who's been dead four years.
The fortress bells rang at the wrong hour three nights running. Nobody will admit to ringing them.
The Maw widened a half-mile east. The surveyors re-drew the map and the map re-drew itself overnight.
A Wyrd-leak opened near the old watchtower and the tower's stones started speaking in Ardweld. Not reciting. Speaking.
A Rider went in with a commission and came back with someone else's memories. He answers to a name that isn't his now.
The Wildfolk at the Maw's edge have stopped manifesting to anyone but children. The children aren't telling adults what they're told.
Something on the far side of the Maw is building. The surveyors can hear the hammering on still nights. The Maw has no far side that anyone can reach.
